organization.description: GitHub organisation that owns every listed repository.

id.description: Folder name under data/ and the URL segment on the site.

enabled.description: Disabled projects are skipped without being removed from the list.

status.description: pre-production means the project has no production environment yet, so production metrics are skipped rather than reported as zero. planned means the repository may not exist yet: only its engineering scorecard is collected, once it does.

production.description: Environment name that counts as production. Names are not standardised across repositories, so this is configuration. null means the project has no production environment, and its production metrics are skipped rather than reported as zero.

staging.description: Environment name that counts as staging.

productionRefPattern.description: Regular expression a production ref should match. Releases that do not match are flagged as out of process rather than excluded.

workflow.description: Workflow that runs the agents, matched on file path first and display name second. The path is preferred because the display name often differs between repositories while the path does not.

ignoreTitlePatterns.description: Run title prefixes that cannot be an agent run, excluded before jobs are fetched purely to save API calls. The kind itself is read from the job named "call-<kind> / agent", so a new kind is discovered without configuration.

engineeringExcellence.description: Reads the engineering excellence facet artifacts (coverage, complexity, mutation, security, sbom) that the repository's own CI uploads. The contract is schema/engineering-excellence-facets.schema.json.

branch.description: Only artifacts uploaded by runs on this branch are read.

artifactPrefix.description: Artifact name prefix. The facet name is appended, so the default reads engineering-excellence-coverage and so on.

roadmap.description: Reads every issue's timeline so the site shows who had each issue at each moment: an agent, a person, the merge gate, or nobody. Needs the token to read pull requests. Meant for repositories where agents and people hand issues over with labels.

labels.description: Label names, only where they differ from the defaults.

working.description: Present while an agent works on the issue.

waiting.description: Present while the issue waits for a person.

stalled.description: The waiting label that means an agent run gave up. Each application counts as one stall.

merge.description: Present while the issue's pull request waits for the merge gate.

triggers.description: Labels that ask an agent to act. An issue that never carried one was worked by hand.

evidenceBranch.description: Branch the evidence workflow commits screenshots and their manifest to, one pr-<number> folder per pull request.

type.description: What kind of project this is, which decides the engineering scorecard practices that apply by default (see types in config/scorecard.json). Absent means other, where every practice applies.

scorecard.description: Per-project overrides for the engineering scorecard.

performance.description: Performance testing (k6, JMeter, Lighthouse CI) is only expected when required. true makes it applicable; false drops it for a type that expects it by default, such as static-site.

notApplicable.description: Practice ids from config/scorecard.json that do not apply to this project, on top of its type's defaults.

reworkLabel.description: Label that marks a pull request as an unplanned fix, feeding deployment rework rate. Defaults to hotfix. A broad label such as bug counts planned backlog fixes as rework and overstates the rate.

reworkLabelPrecision.description: Whether reworkLabel means only unplanned production fixes (incident) or any bug fix (broad). A broad marker is collected and displayed but is not used to place the project on the DORA stability axis, because "released a bug fix" is not the same as "reacted to an incident".

workItemLabel.description: Label marking an issue as work intended to ship, used for the issue to staging measure and the requesters chart. Conventions differ per repository. null reports the metric as not measured rather than as empty.
